Definition: from G5424; to exercise the mind, i.e. entertain or have a sentiment or opinion; by implication, to be (mentally) disposed (more or less earnestly in a certain direction); intensively, to interest oneself in (with concern or obedience):--set the affection on, (be) care(-ful), (be like-, + be of one, + be of the same, + let this) mind(-ed), regard, savour, think.
BiblicalUsage: Phroneo means to think, to mind, to set the mind on something, and Paul makes it the Christian's discipline. Let this mind be in you which was also in Christ Jesus, and be likeminded, having the same love, being of one accord and of one mind. He tells the Romans not to mind high things but to condescend to men of low estate, and says they that are after the flesh do mind the things of the flesh.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe phroneo is the command to choose what my mind feeds on: the mind of Christ, the mind of the flesh, and the mind that minds high things are three different lives. To mind the things of the Spirit is to live by the Spirit, and to be likeminded is to love with one accord. My position is that the battle for my life is fought in my thinking, and Christ's mind is the only one worth having.
